verses.en: Joshua assembled all the Israelite tribes at Shechem. He summoned Israel’s elders, rulers, judges, and leaders, and they appeared before God.

24:1 "Shechem" This was a sacred site for the patriarchs (cf. Gen. 12:6-7; 33:18-20; 35:2-4). Also
it is mentioned later in Deuteronomy 27 and Joshua 8: 30-35. See NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 1213-1216 or ABD,
vol. 5, pp. 1174-1186. Later, Shiloh became the dominate sacred site in the period of the Judges because
of the presence of the tabernacle.

▣ There are several terms that describe leaders within Israel (cf. Jos. 23:2). The exact
meaning of these leadership positions is often speculation:

- Elders, Jos. 8:33; 23:2; 24:1 ‒ BDB 278

- Heads, Jos. 23:2; 24:1 ‒ BDB 910

- Judges, Jos. 8:33; 23:2; 24:1 ‒ BDB 1047

- Officers, Jos. 8:33; 23:2; 24:1 ‒ BDB 1009

verses.zh: 约书亚对众民说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『古时你们的列祖，就是亚伯拉罕和拿鹤的父亲他拉，住在大河那边事奉别神，
verses.en: Joshua told all the people, “This is what the Lord God of Israel has said: ‘In the distant past your ancestors lived beyond the Euphrates River,[NOTE:1] including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor. They worshiped[NOTE:2] other gods,
notes: Heb “the river,” referring to the Euphrates. This has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “served.”
verses.commentary:
24:2 "Joshua said to all the people" He obviously spoke through the officers and the
elders of Jos. 24:2 because the number of people would be too great for him to speak to them all at once.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EXODUS (uncertainties), II. D.

▣ "Thus says the Lord the God of Israel" This is the full
covenant title for deity. Notice the number of "I's" in Jos. 24:1-13. Joshua is speaking directly for
YHWH (cf. Jos. 24:3, 4 (twice), 5 (four), 6, 7, 8 (three), 10 (twice); 1:1,12,13)!

▣ "ancient times" "'Olam" must be interpreted in light of its context. It is
often translated "forever" or "eternal," but this context shows its fluidity (semantic field).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

▣ "the River" This refers to the Euphrates.

▣ "they served other gods" Ur and Haran were both centers of the worship
of the moon goddess. Terah's name (wandering, BDB 1076) itself may reflect this worship.
Abraham was obviously involved to some extent. God chose him in grace, not because of
his theology or unusual merit. The rabbis say he was persecuted by his neighbors because
he was against idolatry. The hero in this text (and all other texts) is YHWH, not the human
beings. The choice of Abraham was an act of pure grace and redemptive purpose
(cf. Gen. 3:15; Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; Luke 22:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

Or “through.”

24:3-4 The VERB "gave" (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) occurs three times in these verses, emphasizing
YHWH's power, control, and eternal purposes.

verses.zh: 又把雅各和以扫赐给以撒，将西珥山赐给以扫为业；后来雅各和他的子孙下到埃及去了。
verses.en: and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I assigned Mount Seir,[NOTE:1] while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
notes: Heb “I gave to Esau Mount Seir to possess it.”
verses.commentary:
24:4 "Mount Seir" This refers to the land south of the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba,
usually associated with Edom. YHWH gave this land to the descendants of Ishmael
(cf. Gen. 16:7-14; 17:18,20).

verses.zh: 我差遣摩西、亚伦，并照我在埃及中所行的降灾与埃及，然后把你们领出来。
verses.en: I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt down when I intervened in their land.[NOTE:1] Then I brought you out.
notes: Heb “by that which I did in its midst.”
verses.commentary: 24:5 Read Gen. 15:12-21. This was purposeful action on YHWH's part.

verses.en: When I brought your fathers out of Egypt, you arrived at the sea. The Egyptians chased your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

verses.zh: 你们列祖哀求耶和华，他就使你们和埃及人中间黑暗了，又使海水淹没埃及人。我在埃及所行的事，你们亲眼见过。你们在旷野也住了许多年日。
verses.en: Your fathers[NOTE:1] cried out for help to the Lord; he made the area between you and the Egyptians dark,[NOTE:2] and then he drowned them in the sea.[NOTE:3] You witnessed with your very own eyes[NOTE:4] what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness for a long time.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the fathers) has been specified in the translation for clarity (see the previous verse).
Or “put darkness between you and the Egyptians.”
Heb “and he brought over them the sea and covered them.”
Heb “your eyes saw.”
Heb “many days.”
verses.commentary:
24:7 "darkness" This cloud represented YHWH's presence, to one, darkness (Egyptians),
to the other, light (Israelis, cf. Exod. 14:19-20). This same word (BDB 66) is used of the ninth
plague on Egypt (i.e., darkness, cf. Exod. 10:22).

verses.zh: 我领你们到约旦河东亚摩利人所住之地。他们与你们争战，我将他们交在你们手中，你们便得了他们的地为业；我也在你们面前将他们灭绝。
verses.en: Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived east of the Jordan. They fought with you, but I handed them over to you; you conquered[NOTE:1] their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
notes: Or “took possession of.”
verses.commentary:
24:8 "the land of the Amorites" This refers to the land east of the Jordan River, which
became the territory of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh (cf. Num. 21:21ff).

verses.zh: 那时，摩押王西拨的儿子巴勒起来攻击以色列人，打发人召了比珥的儿子巴兰来咒诅你们。

notes: Heb “arose and fought.”
Heb “sent and called.”
Or “to curse.”

24:9 "Balak. . .Balaam" This false prophet's attempt to curse Israel (cf. Numbers 22) is
alluded to several times (cf. Deut. 23:4-5; Jos. 13:22; here; Neh. 13:2; Micah 6:5).

▣ "fought against Israel" The UBS Translator's Handbook on Joshua
makes the good point that "fought against Israel" seems to contradict Num. 22:6,11; Deut. 2:9;

verses.zh: 我不肯听巴兰的话，所以他倒为你们连连祝福。这样，我便救你们脱离巴勒的手。
verses.en: I refused to respond to Balaam; he kept[NOTE:1] prophesying good things about[NOTE:2] you, and I rescued you from his power.[NOTE:3]
notes: The infinitive absolute follows the finite verb in the Hebrew text and indicates continuation or repetition of the action. Balaam pronounced several oracles of blessing over Israel (see Num 23-24).
Heb “blessing.” Balaam’s “blessings” were actually prophecies of how God would prosper Israel.
Heb “hand.”
verses.commentary:
24:10 The term translated "bless" is the Piel IMPERFECT and the
Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 138, KB 159), which is a
way to express intensification.

verses.en: I sent terror[NOTE:1] ahead of you to drive out before you the two[NOTE:2] Amorite kings. I gave you the victory; it was not by your swords or bows.[NOTE:3]
notes: Traditionally, “the hornet” (so KJV, NKJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV) but the precise meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain (cf. NEB “panic”).
The LXX has “twelve,” apparently understanding this as a reference to Amorite kings west of the Jordan (see Josh 5:1, rather than the trans-Jordanian Amorite kings Sihon and Og (see Josh 2:10; 9:10).
Heb “and it drove them out from before you, the two kings of the Amorites, not by your sword and not by your bow.” The words “I gave you the victory” are supplied for clarification.
verses.commentary:
24:12 "hornet" This is possibly imagery of divine activity causing fear because,
although it is mentioned several times (cf. Exod. 23:28; Deut. 7:20), it is never listed as
actually happening. The imagery is also used in Deut. 1:44.

purpose of establishing a people who would reflect His character and love to the nations.

19Then Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve the Lord, for He is a holy God. He is a jealous God; He will not forgive your transgression or your sins. 20If you forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods, then He will turn and do you harm and consume you after He has done good to you." 21The people said to Joshua, "No, but we will serve the Lord." 22Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves the Lord, to serve Him." And they said, "We are witnesses." 23Now therefore, put away the foreign gods which are in your midst, and incline your hearts to the Lord, the God of Israel. 24The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the Lord our God and we will obey His voice." 25So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and made for them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem. 26And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the Lord. 27Joshua said to all the people, "Behold, this stone shall be for a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the Lord which He spoke to us; thus it shall be for a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God." 28Then Joshua dismissed the people, each to his inheritance.

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说：「你们不能事奉耶和华；因为他是圣洁的　神，是忌邪的　神，必不赦免你们的过犯罪恶。
verses.en: Joshua warned[NOTE:1] the people, “You will not keep worshiping[NOTE:2] the Lord, for[NOTE:3] he is a holy God.[NOTE:4] He is a jealous God who will not forgive[NOTE:5] your rebellion or your sins.
notes: Heb “said to.”
Heb “you are not able to serve.”
For an excellent discussion of Joshua’s logical argument here, see T. C. Butler, Joshua (WBC), 274-75.

In the Hebrew text both the divine name (אֱלֹהִים, ʾelohim) and the adjective (קְדֹשִׁים, qedoshim, “holy”) are plural. Normally the divine name, when referring to the one true God, takes singular modifiers, but this is a rare exception where the adjective agrees grammatically with the honorific plural noun. See GKC §124.i and IBHS 122.

This assertion obviously needs qualification, for the OT elsewhere affirms that God does forgive. Joshua is referring to the persistent national rebellion against the Mosaic covenant that eventually causes God to decree unconditionally the nation’s exile.tn Heb “lift up” or “take away.”

24:19 "You will not be able to serve the Lord" This follows
the revelation to Moses in Deut. 31:16-22. Joshua seems to be emphasizing the difficulty in
serving a holy God. The sacrificial system of Leviticus was a means for sinful people to approach
a holy God and maintain fellowship (i.e., covenant). It is impossible in our own strength.

(i.e., PLURAL OF MAJESTY), which intensifies the concept.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "jealous God" This (BDB 888) is a love word which implies a deep personal
relationship (cf. Exod. 20:5; 34:14; Deut. 4:24; 5:9; 6:15). He is spoken of as a "father"
or even a "husband" (cf. Hosea 1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

▣ "He will not forgive your transgression or your sins" Covenant obedience
is crucial. God is faithful, but the covenant is conditional. Sin has consequences! YHWH
will not overlook rebellion (cf. Exod. 23:21). This is the problem of the first covenant—fallen
human inability to maintain fellowship with a holy God.

verses.commentary:
24:20 "If" The "if" shows the conditional nature of YHWH's covenant and promises
to Israel (e.g., Deut. 28:1-2,15). All of YHWH's blessings of Deuteronomy 27-28, as well as His
land promises, are conditioned on a faithful, obedient, believing Israel. This is true of the
Old Testament and the eschaton!

verses.en: The people said to Joshua, “No! We really will[NOTE:1] worship[NOTE:2] the Lord.”
notes: The translation assumes that כִּי (ki) is emphatic. Another option is to take it as explanatory, “No, for we will….”

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说：「你们选定耶和华，要事奉他，你们自己作见证吧！」他们说：「我们愿意作见证。」
verses.en: Joshua said to the people, “Do you agree to be witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to worship the Lord?”[NOTE:1] They replied, “We are witnesses!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves the Lord to serve him.”
Like witnesses in a court of law, Israel’s solemn vow to worship the Lord will testify against them in the divine court if the nation ever violates its commitment.
verses.commentary:
24:22 "You are witnesses against yourselves" The covenant has rights and
responsibilities. To say "yes" has definite privileges and consequences. Israel had affirmed
their covenant relationship to YHWH in Jos. 24:16-18 and again in Jos. 24:24.

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「你们现在要除掉你们中间的外邦神，专心归向耶和华―以色列的　神。」
verses.en: Joshua said,[NOTE:1] “Now put aside the foreign gods that are among you and submit to[NOTE:2] the Lord God of Israel.”
notes: The words “Joshua said” are supplied for clarification.
Heb “bend your heart toward.” The term לֵבָב (levav, “heart”) probably here refers to the people’s volition or will.
verses.commentary:
24:23

24:23 "put away the foreign gods which are in your midst" The VERB
"put away" (BDB 693, KB 747) is a Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Jos. 24:14;
Gen. 35:2; 1 Sam. 7:4). The gods were already in their midst (i.e., the Canaanite gods).
Amos 5:27 seems to confirm this possibility, but the second half of the verse implies attitudes,
("incline your hearts," BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE), not
actual objects. This verse calls on Israel to "incline," but 1 Kgs. 8:58 calls on YHWH to
cause His people to "incline" (cf. Prov. 21:1; Psa. 141:4 negated). The Hebrew can mean either.

verses.commentary:
24:27 "it has heard" This is a personification of the stone which was common
(cf. Hab. 2:11; Ezek. 36:4,6). It is characteristic of Hittite treaties for natural objects to act
as witnesses (rocks, trees, clouds, mountains). Joshua has used stones as memorials in
the past (i.e., two piles in Joshua 4).

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 24:32-33

32Now they buried the bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel brought up from Egypt, at Shechem, in the piece of ground which Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for one hundred pieces of money; and they became the inheritance of Joseph's sons. 33And Eleazar the son of Aaron died; and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which was given him in the hill country of Ephraim.

verses.zh: 以色列人从埃及所带来约瑟的骸骨，葬埋在示剑，就是在雅各从前用一百块银子向示剑的父亲、哈抹的子孙所买的那块地里；这就作了约瑟子孙的产业。
verses.en: The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the part of the field that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for 100 pieces of money.[NOTE:1] So it became the inheritance of the tribe of Joseph.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “one hundred qesitahs.” The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (qesitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value and/or weight is unknown. The word occurs only here and in Gen 33:19 and Job 42:11.

Heb “and they became for the sons of Joseph an inheritance.” One might think “bones” is the subject of the verb “they became,” but the verb is masculine, while “bones” is feminine. The translation follows the emendation suggested in the BHS note, which appeals to the Syriac and Vulgate for support. The emended reading understands “the part (of the field)” as the subject of the verb “became.” The emended verb is feminine singular; this agrees with “the part” (of the field), which is feminine in Hebrew.

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare

the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Joshua 24:1-13 is a summary of YHWH's activity toward the man Abraham and his seed.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

- The Hittite treaties of the second millennium B.C. offer us an ancient,
historically contemporary parallel to the structure of Deuteronomy (as well as
Exodus ‒ Leviticus and JosHua 24). This treaty pattern changed by the first
millennium B.C. This gives us evidence for the historicity of the Pentateuch
and Joshua. For further reading in this area, see G. E. Mendenhall's Law and Covenants
in Israel and the Ancient Near East and John Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature in
Its Cultural Context, pp. 95-107.

- The Hittite treaty of the second millennium B.C. and its parallels in Deuteronomy

- preamble (Deut. 1:1-5, introduction of speaker, YHWH)

- review of the past acts of the King (Deut. 1:6-4:49, God's past acts for Israel)

- treaty terms (Deuteronomy 5-26)

- general (Deuteronomy 5-11)

- specific (Deuteronomy 12-26)

- results of treaty (Deuteronomy 27-29)

- benefits (Deuteronomy 28)

- curses/consequences (Deuteronomy 27)

- witness of deity (Deut. 30:19; 31:19, also 32, Moses' song functions as a witness)

- a copy in the temple of the deity

- a copy with the vassal to be read annually

- the uniqueness of the Hittite treaties from the later Assyrian and Syrian treaties were:

(1) the historical review of the past acts of the king

(2) the cursing section was last pronounced

- The Hittite treaty pattern of the second millennium and its parallels in Joshua:

- identification of the King (Jos. 24:2)

- narrative of the King's great acts (Jos. 24:2-13)

- covenant obligations (Jos. 24:14,23)

- instructions for depositing the treaty in the sanctuary (Jos. 24:25-26)

- the deities of the parties involved invoked as witnesses (Jos. 24:22)

- blessing of fidelity; curses for violation (Jos. 24:20)

24:33 "Eleazar" The High Priest during Joshua's day also died and was buried at
Gibeah, not the city in the tribal allocation of Benjamin, but a place near Shiloh in the
allocation of Ephraim.
